prize_parts.citation: for foundational contributions to the analysis of nominal rigidities, price and contract setting, and rule-based monetary policy

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: B015 with Taylor, Calvo and Woodford. My confidence in it as a committee outcome is lower than it was in round 1, because the exchange sharpened the attribution problem. My weighting, which the chair asked members to state separately from any fallback, is conceptual originality, then durability under independent tests, then attribution tractability, then identification quality. On that weighting the B015 core does well on the first two criteria. Calvo supplies the time-dependent pricing device. Taylor supplies staggered contracts and the policy-rule logic. Woodford supplies the microfounded welfare-based synthesis that made monetary policy a normative theory. Each is a separable, originating step, which is the originators-versus-developers distinction the chair asked about. Medium-scale estimation (Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets) and the New Keynesian Phillips curve and its empirical work (Gali) build on these blocks and do not introduce them. The framework has been tested for decades, through 2008 and the 2021-23 inflation. I now word the citation around nominal rigidities, price and contract setting, and rule-based policy in general, not Calvo pricing alone. This takes up Friberg's point that micro price data only partly fit time-dependent pricing. The prize case rests on the organising framework and the policy-rule logic, not on Calvo pricing being literally true of firms. I do not count other members' rankings as scientific evidence. My agreement with the chair is not independent corroboration, as the chair summary notes.
statement.case_against: Attribution is the real weakness, and the round-1 exchange did not remove it. The originators-versus-developers line is a judgement. Andersson and Friberg ranked B015 near the bottom of their opening ballots on exactly this ground, and a framework built cumulatively by at least eight credited contributors fits a three-name cap poorly. The cap may do real injustice to Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler. Micro price-setting evidence and the 2021-23 inflation episode qualify the Calvo-style core, and the representative-agent versions are open to challenge. Earlier macro prizes cover adjacent ground, so marginal novelty is a fair question. B002 has a cleaner credit story. Its weakness is maturity, since the core results are about a decade old and the causal place-effect reading is still contested. If the Committee concludes that B015's attribution cannot be defended, I regard B002 as a legitimate alternative and not a token one. Only two members, both long-time co-authors, explicitly prefer B015, so I do not expect it to reach six votes on present positions.

responses.point: Andersson ranked B015 eighth because attribution is weakest there: eight credited names, a cumulative framework, and a three-name cap that cannot represent its collective origin. He also notes that the 2021-23 inflation experience is debated.
responses.response: I still regard this as the strongest objection to my preferred part, and I have not dismissed it. My position is that a collective origin does not rule out a prize if the foundational steps can be separated. Pricing, contracts and rules, and the normative synthesis can be separated. The estimated and extended versions are a different layer. The cost is that I am asking the Committee to accept a judgement-based cut, and I accept that you may reasonably decline. On the inflation episode, the debate concerns forecasting and the role of supply shocks and slack in the medium-scale models, not the pricing mechanism or rule logic. I also noted that your B004 alternative is attractive precisely because a Kiyotaki-Moore pair attributes cleanly. I regard that cleanness as a real virtue and not a technicality.

responses.point: Friberg would choose the same Calvo-Taylor-Woodford trio but ranks B015 seventh, because micro price data (firm surveys, retail prices) show that time-dependent Calvo pricing fits only partly, and because the cut among at least five other strong contributors is arbitrary.
responses.response: The micro-evidence point changed my citation, not my configuration. I have reworded it around nominal rigidities, price and contract setting, and policy rules in general, so that it does not credit Calvo pricing as a literal description of firm behaviour. The state-dependent and asymmetric adjustment evidence refined the framework and did not displace it. The framework still organises policy analysis, and the refinements work inside it. I concede that this makes the empirical foundation less settled than the policy influence suggests, and that a prize resting on usefulness and organising power is a different claim from one resting on empirical fit. I would not accept the arbitrary-cut point in full, because the three names correspond to distinct building blocks, but I accept that the committee could judge it differently.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B002 first. She argues that population-scale administrative data combined with designs separating place effects from sorting is both new data and a framework, that replication and extension with other administrative datasets answer part of the timing concern, and that the citation should say only what is established.
responses.response: I take this seriously, and it moves me further toward treating B002 as a real alternative. My round-1 hesitation was about maturity and whether the contribution is foundational rather than data-driven. Your answer, that the lasting part is the use of administrative data as a standard and the designs separating place effects from selection, is the best available reply. I cannot check it here, and I rely on your account and the opening files. A citation limited to measurement and exposure-based designs, with no claim about long-run causal effects, would address most of my reservation. What would still concern me is distinguishing the discovery from the oeuvre, and whether the replication outside the US is as extensive as described. I would not oppose a Chetty-Hendren-Friedman prize on principle. I keep B015 ahead because its test of time is longer and its core can be separated more cleanly into steps, not because B002 is lower in quality.

responses.point: Teorell ranks B027 first and ranks B015 third. He argues B027 has a tighter joint core (Persson-Tabellini plus the Besley-Persson state-capacity line) and no comparable attribution problem, while acknowledging that its cross-country identification is less clean than design-based work.
responses.response: I agree that B027 has a more concentrated credit structure than B015, and that is a point against my configuration under the attribution criterion. Where I differ is on how much weight identification should carry. I would treat the framework-versus-evidence trade-off the same way for B027, B015 and B002, and not apply a stricter standard to political economy. You concede that its empirical evidence is weaker than its theory, and I concede the same of Calvo pricing against micro price data. Both are frameworks whose value lies in organising analysis and generating testable implications. That makes me less confident in ranking B015 above B027 on merit than my round-1 file suggested. The difference in my ranking comes mainly from the longer test of time and a more direct link to policy practice. I do not regard the 2024 prize as decisive for B027. As you say, it concerns the origins of institutions and not policy-making rules.

responses.point: Strömberg ranks B004 first with Kiyotaki, Moore and Gertler. He accepts that a Kiyotaki-Moore pair is a defensible fallback and notes that Gertler's credit overlaps with the 2022 prize and with his place on B015.
responses.response: Your point about Gertler's presence on both B004 and B015 matters for my own configuration. It is a reason not to include Gertler in a B015 trio, and my trio leaves him out. It also means the Committee should not credit him twice for overlapping reasons. I did not rank B004 in my opening top eight, so I defer to your account and to Hassler's and Andersson's on whether the collateral-constraint mechanism is well tested. I find the case for the Kiyotaki-Moore pair clean on attribution, and cleaner than my own. I would still weigh the 2022 overlap on novelty, which you also acknowledge.

uncertainties: Whether a three-name cut of an eight-name field can be defended, and whether the originators-versus-developers distinction survives scrutiny, for example in Woodford's case against Gali or Christiano-Eichenbaum.

How much weight the micro price-setting evidence and the 2021-23 inflation experience should carry against a framework whose core is decades old, now that the citation is framed around nominal rigidities and rules in general.

Whether B002's maturity concern would be settled by further replication or long-run follow-up, and whether a measurement-and-exposure-designs citation is enough to meet it. I rely on colleagues' accounts and the supplied files and have not verified the replication evidence.

Whether the committee will accept a configuration with only two explicit supporters, both long-time co-authors, or will move to a cleaner attribution such as B002, B027, or a Kiyotaki-Moore pair in B004.
My assessment rests on general knowledge and the supplied round-1 files, not independent verification of citations or priority claims.
statement.conflict_note: Updated disclosure. No credited name on B015 (Taylor, Calvo, Woodford) appears as a co-author or institutional connection in my profile. I have co-authored with John Hassler (chair), who also prefers B015 and is a long-time IIES colleague, and with Timo Boppart (co-opted member), whose preferred part is B002. Our agreement on B015 should not be read as independent corroboration. I am a long-term co-author of Giovanni Violante (credited on B005, which I do not propose). My work on capital-skill complementarity is adjacent to B024, and my work on heterogeneous-agent methods is adjacent to B005. I serve as secretary. I treat these as disclosures and do not adjudicate them. In this round I weighed Hassler's and Boppart's arguments on their content and did not treat our relationships as evidence of merit.
